title: Conditional Transformation: A Systematic Literature Review of Media Ownership, Digital Audience Engagement, and Regulatory Reform as Drivers of Social Change Under Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030
content: Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030 positions media as both an instrument and an object of national transformation. This systematic literature review synthesizes peer-reviewed evidence published between January 2016 and September 2026 to establish how, and under what conditions, media contribute to social change. In accordance with PRISMA 2020, a search of Open Alex conducted on September 28, 2026, was complemented by scoping searches; 86 studies in journals indexed in Scopus or the Directory of Open Access Journals were appraised on design features adapted from the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool and synthesized thematically across three mechanisms: ownership and investment, digital audience engagement, and regulation. Three convergent patterns emerge. State-led investment and cultural policy have expanded capacity and youth-oriented production across television, film, streaming, gaming, and entertainment, a pattern termed here managed diversification. Platforms have become arenas in which reform, particularly women’s empowerment and flagship national projects, is debated, endorsed, and normalized, with influencers as prominent intermediaries. Regulatory modernization has formalized a fast-growing creator economy, and women’s professional inclusion has advanced, while studies report reliance on official sources and link legal uncertainty and perceived monitoring to anticipatory self-restraint. The review refines the concept of conditional transformation: the communicative visibility of reform has expanded substantially at home and abroad, whereas editorial autonomy has expanded more gradually, and the evidence points to regulatory predictability as a condition for its further expansion. The review maps gaps in political-economy, longitudinal, and reception research and derives recommendations aligned with Vision 2030’s commitment to effective, transparent, and accountable government.
